## Finding

The logs record the transition directly. Through 22:41, `monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations` every minute, with only sporadic `UpstreamTimeout` noise at ~0–2%. At 22:42 — the onset minute — the flag begins evaluating `on` (`off 61 / on 139`), the error signature changes entirely to `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`, and error rate jumps to ~30–42%. No deploys or other changes were recorded in the 24h before onset.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was toggled from off to on at 22:42, and the newly enabled code path on the account page divides by zero (likely an empty/zero spend denominator), producing a sustained ~30-40% error rate. The flag ramped in (off 61 / on 139 in the first minute) and was fully on from 22:43.

supporting_evidence.claim: ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
error_rate jumps from 0.005 at 22:41 to 0.305 at 22:42 with request_volume flat at 1200
Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-14T22:42:00Z to 2026-09-15T22:42:00Z: (nothing changed in this window)

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: a code change shipped without being recorded in the change log introduced the ZeroDivisionError, and the flag log lines merely reflect a coincident rollout. The evidence disfavours this - the change channel shows no deploy in the preceding 24 hours and the error onset aligns minute-for-minute with the flag flip, not with any deploy event.
